finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated query parameter `host` is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters (; | && $() backticks) run arbitrary commands as the server user. The output is returned to the caller.
finding.source: HTTP GET /ping?host=<value> (req.query.host), any remote client; no auth required
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which spawns /bin/sh -c

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping receives the request
req.query.host is concatenated unsanitized into the command string passed to exec (shell)
stdout is sent back to the attacker, so command output is exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or escaping. No authentication or authorization middleware. Not using execFile with an argument array, unlike /version at line 16. req.query.host may also be an array or object via Express query parsing, which is still stringified into the command. The app listens on 3001 with no host restriction. No guard found.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host straight to exec() (shell) with no validation, auth middleware, or allowlist anywhere in the file, and tools.js:11 returns stdout to the caller (output is only returned when the command exits 0, which attackers can arrange, e.g. with `; cmd` or `|| true`).
